title: Dualizing module of a reduced closed subcurve as an annihilator
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ and $Y$ be nonempty proper reduced $k$-schemes of pure dimension one [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension], and let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion with ideal sheaf $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Choose the dualizing modules $\omega_X,\omega_Y$ with their natural representing isomorphisms from [lem-sfb-reduced-curve-dualizing-module]. Then there is a natural isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules
$$i_*\omega_Y\cong\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_X}(i_*\mathcal O_Y,\omega_X)=\{w\in\omega_X:\mathcal Jw=0\}.$$
Here direct image means $(i_*\mathcal G)(U)=\mathcal G(i^{-1}U)$ with its $\mathcal O_X$-action through the structure map, and sheaf Hom is [def-pur-sheaf-hom]; its identification with the displayed annihilator is evaluation at $1$. Neither connectedness of $X,Y$ nor invertibility of $\omega_X,\omega_Y$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0E33 (lemma-closed-immersion-dim-1-CM), (2), for reduced pure-dimensional-one schemes; the annihilator description is evaluation at 1 in the displayed sheaf Hom.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent] to $X$ and $Y$, taking the structure sheaf as the invertible module (basis $1$). Thus both schemes are Noetherian and both structure sheaves are coherent. By [lem-sfb-reduced-curve-dualizing-module], $\omega_X$ and $\omega_Y$ are coherent. Part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence] makes $i_*\mathcal O_Y$ coherent. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-sheaf-hom-coherent] makes $\mathcal H=\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_X}(i_*\mathcal O_Y,\omega_X)$ coherent.

source.place: Tag 0E33 (lemma-closed-immersion-dim-1-CM), (2); ordinary representing-functor proof using Tag 0BS2 (lemma-duality-dim-1), (5)

proof.text: Use the sheaf Hom of [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Evaluation at the unit gives a map $e:\mathcal H\to\omega_X$. Surjectivity in [def-weil-closed-immersion] and the kernel definition in [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] give $i_*\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_X/\mathcal J$ as sheaves. For a local map $f$ and $j\in\mathcal J$, $j f(1)=f(j\cdot1)=0$. Conversely, if a section $w$ is killed by $\mathcal J$, send a local quotient section $\bar a$ to $aw$, choosing lifts locally. Two lifts differ by $\mathcal J$, so these local outputs agree and glue. The formula commutes with restrictions and is linear. A linear map out of the quotient is determined locally by $f(1)$, so these constructions are inverse. Thus $e$ identifies $\mathcal H$ with the annihilator $\operatorname{Ann}_{\omega_X}(\mathcal J)$; in particular $\mathcal J\mathcal H=0$.

source.place: Tag 0E33 (lemma-closed-immersion-dim-1-CM), (2); ordinary representing-functor proof using Tag 0BS2 (lemma-duality-dim-1), (5)

proof.text: Part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence] now supplies a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module $D$ and an isomorphism $i_*D\cong\mathcal H$. For every coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module $G$, the same equivalence gives coherence of $i_*G$ and full faithfulness, hence $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(G,D)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*G,\mathcal H)$. Composing with $e$ gives a bijection from the latter group to $\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*G,\omega_X)$: every map has image killed by $\mathcal J$, since $\mathcal J(i_*G)=0$, and therefore factors uniquely through the annihilator identified in step 2. The inverse is this factorization. These bijections commute with precomposition in $G$ and are $k$-linear.

source.place: Tag 0E33 (lemma-closed-immersion-dim-1-CM), (2); ordinary representing-functor proof using Tag 0BS2 (lemma-duality-dim-1), (5)

proof.text: By [lem-sc-zariski-module-abelian-cohomology-agree] and [lem-sc-cohomology-closed-immersion-pushforward], there is a natural comparison $H^1(X,i_*G)\cong H^1(Y,G)$ for module cohomology. The underlying closed embedding is supplied by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. These comparisons are natural in every module endomorphism, in particular multiplication by each $a\in k$; thus they respect the given $k$-actions. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-curve-dualizing-module] on $X$ to the coherent module $i_*G$. Together with step 3 this gives, naturally in coherent $G$, $$\operatorname{Hom}_Y(G,D)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*G,\omega_X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^1(X,i_*G),k)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^1(Y,G),k).$$

source.place: Tag 0E33 (lemma-closed-immersion-dim-1-CM), (2); ordinary representing-functor proof using Tag 0BS2 (lemma-duality-dim-1), (5)

proof.text: The chosen representing isomorphism on $Y$ in [lem-sfb-reduced-curve-dualizing-module] therefore identifies the last functor with $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(-,\omega_Y)$. Its uniqueness assertion gives $D\cong\omega_Y$. Explicitly, for the resulting natural bijection $T_G:\operatorname{Hom}_Y(G,D)\to\operatorname{Hom}_Y(G,\omega_Y)$, put $u=T_D(1_D)$ and $v=T^{-1}_{\omega_Y}(1_{\omega_Y})$. Naturality says $T_G(f)=u f$ and $T_G^{-1}(g)=v g$, so $uv=1$ and $vu=1$. Pushing this isomorphism forward and composing with step 3 yields $i_*\omega_Y\cong\mathcal H$. Step 2 identifies its right side with the displayed annihilator. The formulas use only the chosen representing isomorphisms and the quotient map, so respect isomorphisms of those choices. No connectedness or invertibility of a dualizing module was used.

Statement: Stacks curves.tex 0E33 (lemma-closed-immersion-dim-1-CM)(2), specialized to nonempty proper reduced curves of pure dimension one with the H^1-representing modules of lem-sfb-reduced-curve-dualizing-module (0BS2(5)/0BS3). It is true, and the ordinary adjunction argument proves it. Step 1: lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent with N=O gives Noetherian and O coherent; that makes 087T(1) applicable and gives i_*O_Y coherent; 01CQ gives sheaf Hom coherent. Step 2: Hom(O_X/J, ω) equals Ann_ω(J) by evaluation at 1, using local lifts and gluing correctly. Step 3: the essential image of 087T(1) is the J-killed coherent modules, which gives D; the bijection Hom_Y(G,D) to Hom_X(i_*G, ω_X) is correct. Step 4: 02UV uses topological cohomology, which def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology identifies with Zariski cohomology; 03FD then gives module cohomology on both X and Y; k-linearity follows from naturality. Step 5: the Yoneda argument works within coherent O_Y-modules and agrees with the uniqueness clause. Edge cases checked: i=id; a union of connected components; the node xy=0 with Ann(x)=(y); non-Gorenstein curves and arbitrary k. lem-sfb-nodal-subcurve-dualizing-annihilator is a nodal, algebraically-closed special case with a different ω, not a duplicate; advisory only. Batch-5: lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent is a generic Stacks 01XZ/01T6 fact that the parent already cites; it is not part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality and neither assumption gives it, so the citation is accepted. The generic cross-unit cites in split_report.tool_uses (087T, 01CQ, 02UV, 03FD, 01XZ) are accepted.
